title: Green sea turtles
text:
Green sea turtles are large reptiles. They live in warm seas all around the world, including the seas around Indonesia.

What do they look like?
A green sea turtle has a smooth, hard shell and four strong flippers. A fully grown turtle can be more than a metre long and heavier than a grown-up person. It is named after the green colour of the fat under its shell. The shell itself is mostly brown or olive.

What do they eat?
Young turtles eat lots of different foods, such as jellyfish and crabs. Adults mostly eat seagrass and seaweed.

Laying eggs
A mother turtle swims back to the beach where she hatched. At night, she crawls up the sand and digs a hole with her back flippers. She lays about 100 eggs, covers them with sand and returns to the sea. About two months later, the baby turtles hatch and scurry down to the water.

Helping turtles
Baby turtles find the sea by heading for the brightest part of the sky, which is usually over the water. Bright lights from buildings can lead them the wrong way. In Indonesia, some nesting beaches, such as Sukamade in East Java, are protected so that turtles can lay their eggs safely.
